column1: # The one record of what actually ran in a host. Every prose claim about a host
# has to agree with a row here; `tools/check-docs.py` reads this file and fails a
# document that says a host with a row has never run something.

column7: default gain; mae 0.0 and max 0 over 8294400 bytes, so the frame is the source to the byte (the .log beside it prints only the frame size)
gain 2.0; mae 0.0 and max 0 against the doubled source; 1920x1080 PNG is the source times two to the byte, so render() ran
mae 0.0 over 8294400 bytes; the declaration names the CUDA path for all eight invocations
host killed with a job in flight; the run ends fail with the host exit code in 47 s
tier 3 of verify-bundle.bat with the GPU processing mode on Auto; the host logs "Compute API set to automatic, defaulting to CUDA", the effect is applied and one 1920x1080 frame decodes
the same tier with the mode set to CUDA; the log carries "Selected compute API: CUDA" and no automatic line, and the preference was restored afterwards
one 256x256 frame through testkit/verify-bundle.bat, pixels checked

the host hands over no OpenCL queue: nine render() calls arrive with opencl=0 and a null pOpenCLCmdQ (eight 1920x1080 frames and one 208x117 preview window), and the frame is the source times 2.0 to the byte; the host is in CUDA mode, so it offers CUDA buffers, not an OpenCL queue

describe() accepts every write the template makes except kOfxImageEffectPropCPURenderSupported; with that one guarded, the host instantiates the effect, creates the filter context and renders 1920x1080 with the model's output - mae 94.87 against the source, and mae 0.198 of 255 (max 0.5) against the same model run on the CPU (onnx-describe-resolve.log)

the provider-only bundle, both packages: the host registers the bundle and the effect is on the timeline, but no instance is ever created - 19 create-context failures at 18:55 with the 1.32.0 package and 151 at 18:58 with the 1.20.1 one - and the frame is the source (mae 0.0) with ONNX_MODEL_PATH pointing at test_conv.onnx; the plug-in's describe() is the cause, guarded on 2026-11-27 (onnx-describe-resolve.log)
